## Prerequisites

<details class="q" id="what-are-the-course-prerequisites"><summary>What are the course prerequisites?</summary>

Like all courses at IIT Gandhinagar, the course has no formal prerequisites. It assumes a basic understanding of programming in Python.

</details>

<details class="q" id="what-is-the-prerequisite-exam"><summary>What is the prerequisite exam?</summary>

An exam designed to make sure you have the background needed for the course.

</details>

<details class="q" id="how-can-i-prepare-for-the-prerequisite-exam"><summary>How can I prepare for the prerequisite exam?</summary>

Your undergraduate course material should be enough.

</details>

<details class="q" id="what-happens-if-i-do-not-clear-the-prerequisite-exam"><summary>What happens if I do not clear the prerequisite exam?</summary>

You will not be allowed to take the course.

</details>

<details class="q" id="what-does-clear-the-exam-mean"><summary>What does "clear" the exam mean?</summary>

As in all courses at IIT Gandhinagar, the instructor decides the cut-off, and you must score above it. The cut-off is not revealed to students beforehand.

</details>

## Laptops

<details class="q" id="can-i-use-my-laptop-or-phone-in-class"><summary>Can I use my laptop or phone in class?</summary>

No, not for any reason, unless it is a lab session where the instructor has explicitly allowed laptops.

</details>

## Quizzes

<details class="q" id="what-if-i-miss-a-quiz"><summary>What if I miss a quiz?</summary>

- The quiz is marked 0.
- The best 3 of 4 rule is designed for such cases.

</details>

<details class="q" id="are-quizzes-open-book"><summary>Are the quizzes and the end-semester exam open book? Can I carry notes?</summary>

No. Exams and quizzes are closed book, and you may not carry notes.

</details>

<details class="q" id="when-do-i-get-my-answer-sheets-back"><summary>When do I get my answer sheets back?</summary>

Within 4 to 5 working days.

</details>

<details class="q" id="is-there-a-mid-semester-or-end-semester-exam"><summary>Is there a mid-semester or end-semester exam?</summary>

Two of the four quizzes are held in the mid-semester and end-semester exam slots. The other two are held during the semester.

</details>

<details class="q" id="are-quizzes-multiple-choice"><summary>Are the quizzes multiple-choice or written?</summary>

They may contain both multiple-choice and written questions.

</details>

## Assignments

<details class="q" id="what-if-i-miss-an-assignment"><summary>What if I miss an assignment?</summary>

There are no extensions for assignments.

</details>

<details class="q" id="whom-do-i-ask-about-an-assignment"><summary>I have a doubt about an assignment. Whom should I ask?</summary>

Ask on the #assignments channel on Slack. If you get no response within 2 days, write to the course instructor.

</details>

<details class="q" id="can-i-use-another-language"><summary>I do not know Python. Can I write assignments in another language?</summary>

No. Assignments must be in Python.

</details>

<details class="q" id="how-are-assignments-evaluated"><summary>How are assignments evaluated?</summary>

Each assignment is followed by a viva. The TAs first check the code against the submission; any change from the submitted code is not allowed and leads to a warning. The TAs then run the code and ask a few questions: about 75% on the assignment and about 25% on the theory behind the concepts it covers.

The marks are split as follows: the code runs correctly and solves the problem (50%); questions on the assignment and your understanding of the code (25%); code quality (12.5%); questions on the theory (12.5%).

</details>

<details class="q" id="are-assignments-individual-or-group"><summary>Are assignments individual or group?</summary>

Group. All team members get the same grade for the assignment.

</details>

## Attendance

<details class="q" id="attendance-policy"><summary>What is the attendance policy?</summary>

See [Attendance](assessment.qmd#attendance) and [Leave](assessment.qmd#leave) on the Assessment page.

</details>

## Auditing

<details class="q" id="can-i-audit-the-course"><summary>Can I audit the course?</summary>

You are free to attend the lectures. However, with a limited number of TAs and a large number of students, your submissions cannot be graded, and you cannot formally contribute to a team's assignments.

</details>

## Computational resources

<details class="q" id="computational-resources"><summary>Will we get cloud credits?</summary>

Google has typically provided cloud credits, which are more than enough for the assignments. This section was to be updated once the credits were available.

</details>
